thread_title: S. leucophylla var. alba 'best of batch' Baldwin Co, AL
breadcrumb: S. leucophylla var. alba 'best of batch' Baldwin Co, AL

posts.body_html:
It was the best of batch....it was the worst of batch! Well, actually, it's definitely not the worst of the batch, just sounds catchy to remix a tale of two cities (by Charles Dickens) Sarracenia style!

Yes, this was the best plant out of maybe 100+ in the batch, hence the name. It was the only one that was blindingly white, which made it stand out of the crowd. Given its chameleon genetics, it doesn't always appear alba-ey, but this year(so far) it's looking quite white.

So the pitchers aren't very showy right now being that these are late summer traps, but you can definitely tell, this thang is very alba-esque! It feels like November here on the San Francisco Bay Area, CA Peninsula, with highs in the 60's and lows in the low to mid 50's, so most of the growth that we normally get right now is on hold. Nevertheless, there's still a lil sum'in sum'in to look at. Photos taken 8/18/18:


as mentioned earlier, this clone is very chameleon-like:





To be continued....if the darn fall traps ever come up! LOL

posts.body_html:
This clone is quite difficult to tease out the alba from it, and it has performed in the past, just haven't photographed it in all its glory. Right now, it's still not at its fullest potential, but to the seasoned eye, you can tell this clone has some serious alba genes in it and can get very white if the environment is just right!

Some updated pics, taken 11/3/22:


Check out the trap to the left, the same exact clone! If all you saw was that trap, you probably wouldn't believe this is an alba! My whitest, most easy to color up clone in the collection does this as well: it has produced regular looking traps depsite being snow white most of the time:
